documented_impact: Crop/livestock sensitivity and household coping pressures.
fcv_mediator: Income and food-security loss; market dependence; depletion of assets.
possible_consequence: Where households lack alternatives, livelihood deterioration could increase displacement, grievance, harmful coping or susceptibility to wider instability.
uncertainty: Complete climate -> violence chain is not demonstrated.
compact_statement: Climate stress can worsen livelihood insecurity, but any FCV effect is mediated by markets, assets, governance and conflict conditions rather than being automatic. (UNFCCC2)

climate_pressure: Drought, rainfall variability, heat and changing pasture/water availability.
documented_impact: Pressure on livestock systems and possible altered seasonal movements.
fcv_mediator: Migration timing, livestock corridors, land access, water points and farmer-herder institutions.
possible_consequence: Earlier or redirected livestock movement may raise localized conflict risks where crops, routes or water points overlap and governance mechanisms fail.
uncertainty: Climate-specific contribution relative to these drivers is poorly quantified.
resilience_factors: customary dispute mechanisms and locally designed resource governance
compact_statement: Climate variability may modify pastoral mobility and resource contact, but governance and political-security conditions determine whether such contact becomes conflictual. (CGSpace9)

climate_pressure: Drought, heat, flood or rainfall failure/variability.
documented_impact: Potential livelihood loss and climate-sensitive migration.
fcv_mediator: Movement into areas with constrained land, services and employment.
possible_consequence: Host-area tension could increase where access and institutions are inadequate.
alternative_explanations: The current displacement crisis is primarily a direct consequence of war and violence
uncertainty: Very high for any attempt to allocate current displacement quantitatively to climate.
compact_statement: Climate-sensitive livelihood mobility is plausible, but Sudan's current mass displacement must not be attributed to climate without direct evidence. (NUPI8)

climate_pressure: Background climate variability may affect production, but it is not the initiating pressure in this pathway.
documented_impact: Siege, blocked roads, destroyed water infrastructure, disrupted planting and markets.
possible_consequence: Households can lose assets, nutrition and coping capacity, leaving them more susceptible to later drought, heat, floods and disease.
alternative_explanations: Macroeconomic collapse and pre-existing poverty interact strongly
uncertainty: Future climate consequences of depleted coping capacity are inferred.
compact_statement: In current conflict zones, armed violence and access constraints are demonstrably undermining the production, food and service systems on which climate resilience depends. (IPCinfo5)

climate_pressure: Multiple existing and future climate hazards.
documented_impact: Federal implementation capacity is unreliable in current World Bank project arrangements; state/local structures and third-party actors carry delivery functions.
fcv_mediator: Conflict, institutional fragmentation, security constraints and reduced fiscal resources.
possible_consequence: Climate adaptation, WASH, agriculture, health and early-warning investments may be delayed, uneven or inaccessible.
alternative_explanations: Pre-war underinvestment and capacity deficiencies already existed
uncertainty: Project evidence cannot establish equal levels of impairment in every state.
compact_statement: War compounds pre-existing adaptation-capacity gaps and shifts delivery toward decentralized and humanitarian structures. (UNFCCC2)

climate_pressure: Future drought, heat and rainfall variability.
documented_impact: Darfur evidence indicates conflict accelerated environmental degradation and weakened traditional environmental-management arrangements.
fcv_mediator: Armed violence, institutional erosion, displacement and contested resource governance.
possible_consequence: Degraded land and governance could leave livelihoods less able to absorb later climate shocks.
uncertainty: Foundational source is old; environmental degradation cannot automatically be attributed to climate.
resilience_factors: Restored customary/resource institutions and conflict-sensitive ecosystem rehabilitation
compact_statement: Conflict can undermine the ecological and governance assets needed for later adaptation, but the evidence is Darfur-specific and partly historical. (Humanitarian Practice Network12)

documented_impact: Water access is a recurring livelihood and resource-management concern.
fcv_mediator: Whether infrastructure and access are shared, governed and perceived as legitimate.
possible_consequence: Jointly managed water systems could reduce friction and support community stabilization.
alternative_explanations: New water infrastructure can itself generate distributional disputes if siting
ownership or recharge is poorly managed
uncertainty: No identified evaluation demonstrates a peace outcome in the current war context.
compact_statement: Water projects are potentially peace-supporting only when their governance and distribution are conflict-sensitive; infrastructure alone is not evidence of peace impact. (Climate-Diplomacy4)

documented_impact: A pre-war programme delivered climate information, insurance and finance-related adaptation activities and received generally positive terminal-evaluation ratings.
fcv_mediator: Household capacity to manage shocks without distress asset sales, displacement or severe consumption cuts.
possible_consequence: Better financial and information capacity could reduce erosive coping and therefore some forms of fragility exposure.
uncertainty: No peace/conflict outcome was evaluated; programme predates April 2023.
resilience_factors: sustained funding and accessible advisory services
compact_statement: Climate-information and risk-finance programmes show adaptation potential, but no verified evidence establishes that they reduced conflict or survived current-war disruption. (UNDP IEO Evaluation Resource Center11)
